resolved.title: 字典
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Dictionaries[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

We saw how [b]lists[/b] allow us to store elements with their corresponding indices.
The indices in a list are automatically set. But what if we need to set our own index?

[b]Dictionaries [/b]are another collection type and allow us to map arbitrary [b]keys[/b] to [b]values[/b].
Dictionaries can be indexed in the same way as lists, using [b]square brackets[/b] containing keys.

[s0l0!-header][b]Example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="359"]ages = {
   "Dave": 24,
   "Mary": 42,
   "John": 58
}
print(ages["Dave"])
print(ages["Mary"])[/code]
[note]Each element in a dictionary is represented by a [b]key:value[/b] pair.[/note]

resolved.title: 字典

content.text:
你可以使用字符串、整数、布尔运算和任何其他 **不可变的** 类型作为字典的键。
这意味着你不能使用列表或字典作为键。
content.text_html:
You can use strings, integers, booleans, and any other immutable type as dictionary keys. This means that you cannot use lists or dictionaries as keys:

你可以使用字符串、整数、布尔运算和任何其他不可变的类型作为字典的键。 这意味着你不能使用列表或字典作为键。
